_doc: Amane conversation tree (GDD 4.3, CAST.md). A talk = opener -> pick a TOPIC (menu) -> Amane's line (a) -> pick one of the REPLIES (exact words) -> his answer (say) + feeling + effects. Up to 3 topics per talk, each once per day. tone defaults (amane.gd TONE_FX): kind, flirt, tease, curious, honest, boundary, cold, lie; fx overrides; lore = sets a past-life / town lore flag (Notes tab). when = requirements: min_bond, min_trust, min_self, min_day, min_tears, max_tears, route, not_route, rival, stage_min, lore, no_lore, period, dusk. {player} {rival} work everywhere.
again: "You asked me that {when}, Senpai." He tilts his head. "...It's okay. I like answering you."
"Senpai asked me that {when}." A tiny frown. "Were you not listening? ...I'll say it again. Slower."
He blinks. "You asked the same thing {when}. Do you want a different answer? I only have the one."
"Again?" He hides a smile in his sleeve. "You asked {when}. Maybe you just like hearing me talk."
"I told you {when}." His ears droop a little. "You forget things. I know. I'll remember for both of us."
"That's the same question as {when}." He thinks. "...My answer's the same. Mostly."

0: Okay! I'll be... around. Not following. Around.
See you, Senpai. (He doesn't move until you're out of sight.)
4: Don't go-- I mean. Go. It's fine. *it is not fine*

a: It always rains when I... It's just the season, Senpai.
Grandma says when a cat washes its face, it rains. I don't wash my face that much.

replies.t: "I like the rain. Everything goes quiet."
say: ...Really? Then I'll stop feeling bad about it. A little.
Quiet is nice. You can hear people breathing. I mean-- the rain. You can hear the rain.
*His ears pop out.* W-what? No! That's-- who told you that? Was it a cat?
...If I said yes, would you think I'm weird? Weirder?

replies.t: "Share my umbrella? It's big enough for two."
say: *He stands so close your shoulders touch. The rain stops. Just over the two of you.*
Big enough for two. You said two. You said it.

replies.t: "Could you stand a bit further away?"
say: ...Further. Okay. Is here good? ...Here? I'll learn the right distance, Senpai.
...Oh. I'll go be annoying somewhere else.
say_crying: *The rain gets louder. He doesn't say anything at all.*

a: Rice. And tamagoyaki. And grilled mackerel. Too much mackerel. I always make too much fish.
I made it for me. There's just extra. Exactly one Senpai-sized extra.

say: *He watches every bite like it's the last scene of a movie.*
You ate the fish first. You always ate the fish first.

replies.t: "Did you get up at five to make this?"
say: Four-thirty. I mean-- no. Normal time. Normal person time.
T-together?! I'll get a mat! I have a mat. I always carry a mat. In case.

replies.t: "You can't make me lunch every day."
say: ...Every other day?
Okay. Mondays and Thursdays. Final offer.
Strangers... Right. We're strangers. *He closes the lid very carefully.*

a: It's not against the rules. Not exactly. Makabe-sensei gave up.
It has a hood. For when I need to not be looked at. Which is always, except by you.

say: *He pulls the strings until only his nose shows.* ...Thank you.

replies.t: "What are you hiding under the hood?"
say: N-nothing! Hair. Normal hair. Normal amount of ears. Two. Human ones. Bye.

replies.t: "Can I borrow it when it's cold?"
say: *You have never seen anyone take off a hoodie that fast.*
Keep it. Forever. I have four more.

replies.t: "You don't need to hide from everyone."
say: ...People look at me like I'm a ghost. You look at me like I'm a person. That's the only kind of looking I can stand.
...I know. I know I'm creepy. You don't have to say it.

a: Grandma tied it on me when I was a baby. I've never taken it off. Not even in the bath.
It's old. Older than the shrine stairs, Grandma says. It used to belong to... someone.

say: ...So I can always find my way back. That's what Grandma said.

replies.t: "Who did it belong to before you?"
say: To a cat. A long time ago. The shrine's cat. ...The town prayed to it, after. And then it was mine. Don't laugh.

replies.t: "I like the sound. I always know you're near."
say: *He jingles it. Twice. Very quietly.* ...That one meant hello.
It only rings when I want it to. Mostly. Except when I'm upset. Then it doesn't ring at all.
*He covers it with both hands like you tried to grab it.* No. Anything else. Not this.

a: They're not following me. We just go to the same places. Every place.
Cats are good listeners. They hear everything. Then they tell... nobody. Cats don't talk, Senpai.

replies.t: "They like you. Cats have good taste."
say: ...You're the only person who ever said that like it was a good thing.

replies.t: "Do the cats tell you about me?"
say: *Long pause.* ...What a strange question. Ha. Ha ha. Don't pet the grey one by the vending machine. He's a gossip.

replies.t: "I'd follow you around too, if I were a cat."
say: S-Senpai would be a terrible cat. Too loud. Too warm. I'd let you sit on me anyway.

replies.t: "Tell your cats to give me some privacy."
say: ...I'll ask them. They don't listen to me either.
*Every cat on the street turns its head toward you at the same time.*

a: Fine. Quiet. Nobody sits next to me. It's very spacious.
They call me 'the rain boy'. It's not a mean name. It's just a true name.

replies.t: "Want me to walk you to class tomorrow?"
say: Yes. I mean-- if it's on your way. It isn't. I'll pretend it is.

replies.t: "You should join a club. The library committee needs people."
say: A club... with people in it. ...If Senpai thinks I can. I'll try. Once.
*He looks at you like you hung the moon.* ...You'd sit with me?
When I was little I told them about things I remembered. Old things. Nobody wanted to sit near me after that.
...Maybe they do.

a: Grandma Chiyo. She runs the shrine. She feeds every cat in Suzunari and scolds every human.
She's strict. She says I have to be careful who I love. Who says that to a kid?

replies.t: "She sounds like she loves you a lot."
say: ...She does. She just says it like a rule.

replies.t: "Why does she say to be careful who you love?"
say: Because in our family, it's only ever once. That's the rule of the shrine. ...Forget I said that.
She'd hit you with her cane. Then make you tea. That's approval.
She already knows who you are. She knew the day your train came in. ...I don't know how either.
...Yeah. It is. You don't have to stick around for it.

a: Dad left when I was three. Mom... went up the shrine steps on Tanabata when I was one. She didn't come down.
People say she ran away. Grandma says she went to ask someone for something. For me.

say: *He nods, very small.* ...You're the first person who said sorry instead of 'how weird'.
Grandma says there are courts. Past the steps. Where they decide what you have to pay for. Mom went to pay for me. ...It sounds crazy out loud.

replies.t: "Then I'll stay. I won't go up those steps without you."
say: *He grabs your sleeve and doesn't let go for a long time.*
...On Tanabata nights I hear a woman humming on the stairs. Nobody else hears it. I think she's waiting. Like I did.
*The bell on his collar goes completely silent.*

steps.menu: "Why shouldn't I count the shrine steps?"
a: There are nine hundred and ninety-nine. If you count at dusk and get a thousand... don't keep walking. Please.
The steps were built after a tsunami. People ran up them and counted them so they'd stay brave. Some of them never stopped counting.

say: *He holds out his pinky. Then pulls it back.* No. No pinky promises. I'll just... trust you.
Dusk. Forever. A festival that never ends. People who are still waiting for someone. ...You were there once. You don't remember.

replies.t: "Walk them with me at sunset. I'll count, you hold my hand."
say: ...If you're holding my hand, I won't let you get to a thousand. I'll pull you back. I'm stronger than I look.
Every summer since I was five. I always get nine hundred and ninety-nine. I'm waiting for the year I get a thousand.
...Then count them. Go on. See if I come after you this time.

a: Nine summers ago. You were seven. You got lost on the steps. I walked you down. You said 'next summer'. Then you never came back.
You hooked your pinky around mine. You said if you lied you'd swallow a thousand needles.

replies.t: "I'm sorry. I don't remember. But I'm here now."
say: *He laughs and cries at the same time. Somewhere, the sun comes out while it's still raining.*
You're here now. ...Say it again. Slowly.

replies.t: "Why did a seven-year-old get lost on shrine steps?"
say: You weren't lost. You were walking up like someone called you. You counted to a thousand. You were gone a whole night. I'm the one who went in after you.
*His pinky finds yours. The bell rings once, loud, like a door opening.*
It counts. Words count, Senpai. In this town, words count more than anything.

replies.t: "You've been waiting nine years for that? That's creepy."
say: Nine years is nothing. ...I've waited longer. Much longer. You wouldn't believe me.

dreams.menu: "Do you ever dream about the past?"
a: I dream I'm small and furry and sitting on a cold stone step. Every night. For years.
Sometimes I dream of a hill. Mud and rain and a man saying 'I'll be late'. I wake up so angry. Then so sad.

replies.t: "I dream of that hill too. The rain. The mud."
say: *He stares at you for a very long time.* ...Then you were really there. Then it was really you.

replies.t: "The man on the hill... who was he?"
say: Someone who left in eighteen sixty-eight and said he'd come back by next Tanabata. He came back twenty-two years late. I'd already--. ...Forget it.
I do. That's the problem. ...Was that out loud?
...Okay. Tonight I'll dream about something normal. Like fish.
Maybe. It's warmer than here.

a: Everything. No. Something. Why did you come to Suzunari, Senpai? The real reason.
Do you like it here? Be honest. If you don't like it I'll fix it. I'll fix the whole town.

replies.t: "My grandfather's will. I have to live here until I'm eighteen."
say: Until eighteen... That's next Tanabata. Your grandpa knew. He always knew.
Then I'll pretend I don't know you. ...I can't. Sorry. I'll be quiet about it.

replies.t: "I think I came here for you."
say: *All the strength goes out of his knees. He sits down on the pavement.* ...Give me a minute.

replies.t: "I like the cats. And the sweets. And the quiet."
say: Cats, sweets, quiet. I'm writing it down. *He is actually writing it down.*
...Right. Sorry. I'll find out from the cats.

a: Who's {rival} to you, Senpai? I'm just asking. Everyone's allowed to ask.
You laughed with {rival} at lunch. Thirty-one seconds. I wasn't counting.

replies.t: "{rival}'s my friend. You can be friends with him too."
say: Friends with {rival}... *He tries to imagine it. His face does something complicated.* ...I'll try to say hello.
N-no! Jealousy is for people who-- *the bell goes quiet* --who aren't sure. I'm very sure.

replies.t: "You're the only one I wait for after school."
say: *The tension drains out of him like rain off a roof.* ...Okay. Okay. Then nothing needs to happen to anyone.
...I'm not doing anything to {rival}. I'm asleep at night. I'm always asleep. *He doesn't look at you.*

replies.t: "Who I hang out with isn't your business."
say: You're right. It isn't. ...It's the cats' business.

blackcat.menu: "Have you seen a black cat with two tails?"
a: Two tails? Cats only have one. Everybody knows that. Why are you asking me?
I sleep very deeply, Senpai. I don't know anything about the nights. I dream, that's all.

replies.t: "I think it's you, Amane. And I think you don't know."
say: *He goes white.* ...Every morning my feet are dirty. Every morning there's fur on my pillow. I thought I was going crazy.

replies.t: "Whatever happens at night, I'm not angry with you."
say: ...If I hurt someone in my sleep, would you still say that?
Then tonight I'll try to dream about something kind.

replies.t: "Stay at my place tonight. I'll keep watch."
say: *He turns the colour of a red lantern.* S-Senpai's aunt would-- I'll bring a futon. A separate futon. Very separate.

replies.t: "If anything happens to {rival}, I'll know it was you."
say: ...Then nothing will happen. I'll hold on. I promise I'll hold on.
*He doesn't cry. That's the scariest part. He just nods, and walks away, and every cat on the street follows him.*

festival.menu: "Are you going to the Tanabata festival?"
a: I go every year. I sit on the shrine steps and watch the lanterns. Alone. It's tradition.
You write a wish on a paper strip and hang it on the bamboo. I've written the same wish nine times.

say: *He nods so hard his bell jingles.* I'll wear a yukata. Grandma's going to cry. I'm going to cry. You're going to see a lot of crying.
For someone to come home. ...It's a boring wish. Don't laugh.

replies.t: "Let's go as a group. Hayate, Hina, you, me."
say: A group. With... people. ...If you're there, I can stand people.

replies.t: "Write a wish for yourself this year. Not for anyone else."
say: For myself? ...I don't know what I want, except-- No. I'll think about it. Properly.
...Then I'll sit on the steps alone. Like always. It's fine. I'm good at alone.

a: Fish. Any fish. Raw fish. Grilled fish. Fish someone dropped. I'm joking. Mostly.
Taiyaki. It's a fish, but it's a cake. It's perfect. It's the perfect object.

replies.t: "Let's get taiyaki after school. My treat."
say: After school. Taiyaki. Your treat. I'm going to remember this sentence for a hundred years.
*Very long silence.* ...I don't know what you mean. *He is holding a fish-shaped cracker.*

replies.t: "I'll learn to grill mackerel. For you."
say: For me. Mackerel. *He has to hold onto a lamppost.*
...Vegetables. For you I'll eat one carrot. One. Witness it.
...Oh. I'll stop eating fish near you. I'll stop eating fish.

a: He's loud. He smells like a dog. He walks you home every day like it's his job.
The dog shrine boy. Our families don't talk. Grandma says the dogs walk the dead home and the cats just... wait.

replies.t: "He's a good guy. You'd like him."
say: ...He gave me half his melon bread once. I threw it at him. I regret it a little.

replies.t: "Dogs walk the dead home? What does that mean?"
say: Okuri-inu. Night-walking dogs. If you fall, they eat you. If you pretend you're resting, they walk you home. ...One walked someone home for thirteen years once.

replies.t: "Don't worry. I like cats more than dogs."
say: *He looks like he just won the lottery and the war at the same time.*
I'm always nice. I'm nice to everyone. ...I'll be nicer. On purpose.
...Then go walk home with Hayate. He's good at it.
